mainEntity.name: How do I know if a dentist is qualified to place dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the UK, all dentists must be GDC-registered, but implant placement requires additional postgraduate training beyond the standard dental degree. Look for evidence of formal implant training, membership of professional bodies such as the ADI or BAIRD, and ongoing CPD in implant dentistry. You can verify GDC registration directly through the GDC website. It is also entirely reasonable to ask your prospective dentist about their implant training and experience during your consultation.

mainEntity.name: What should be included in a dental implant consultation?

acceptedAnswer.text: A responsible implant consultation should include a full review of your dental and medical history, a clinical examination of your teeth, gums, and bite, and discussion of diagnostic imaging requirements — often including a CBCT scan. The dentist should explain all stages of treatment, discuss risks and alternatives, and provide a written treatment plan before you make any decisions. A consultation that does not include a clinical examination cannot provide a reliable treatment recommendation.

Not everyone is immediately suitable for dental implants, and suitability can only be confirmed through clinical assessment. Factors such as insufficient bone volume, active gum disease, uncontrolled systemic health conditions, and smoking can affect both suitability and healing. In some cases, preparatory treatment such as bone grafting or gum disease management can make implants possible. Your dentist will discuss your individual situation during assessment.

mainEntity.name: What is peri-implantitis and how can it be prevented?

acceptedAnswer.text: Peri-implantitis is an inflammatory condition affecting the gum and bone around a dental implant, often caused by bacterial build-up. It can lead to bone loss around the implant if left unmanaged. Prevention involves thorough daily oral hygiene around the implant, use of interdental brushes or implant floss, regular professional hygiene appointments, and avoiding smoking. Early signs — such as gum swelling or bleeding around the implant — should be reviewed by a dental professional promptly.

mainEntity.name: How long do dental implants last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dental implants are designed as a long-term tooth replacement option, and with appropriate care, many function well for many years. However, longevity depends on individual factors including bone quality, oral hygiene, general health, and lifestyle habits such as smoking. No outcome can be guaranteed, and individual results vary. Regular dental monitoring and maintenance appointments are important in supporting implant longevity over time.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to travel abroad for cheaper dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dental tourism is a personal decision, but there are important considerations. If complications arise after returning to the UK, ongoing care may be complex, costly, and difficult to coordinate. Pre-treatment assessments, follow-up appointments, and management of any concerns are more straightforward when your treating clinician is accessible. It is worth weighing the full cost — including potential return trips and aftercare — when comparing options. Clinical standards, regulatory frameworks, and implant systems used can also vary significantly between countries.
